literal: His son Gongdao was mild and good-natured by temperament and possessed considerable literary accomplishment.
idiomatic: His son Gongdao was gentle by nature and well versed in letters.

literal: The province recruited him as chief clerk.
idiomatic: The province recruited him as chief clerk.

literal: When Li Chong marched north on campaign, he was appointed ink-and-record staff officer of an opened government office.
idiomatic: When Li Chong marched north on campaign, Gongdao was made ink-and-record staff officer to his opened government office.

literal: From the time Wenwei held Fanyang, through repeated invasions and calamities, Gongdao often helped his father in defense.
idiomatic: From the time Lu Wenwei held Fanyang, through raid after raid, Gongdao often stood at his father's side in defense.

literal: Guo Xiu, minister of the seven armories, had long been on intimate terms with Gongdao; once he took office, he repeatedly praised and recommended him, and the Grand Ancestor also heard his name.
idiomatic: Guo Xiu, minister of the seven armories, had long been close to Gongdao; once in power, he spoke of him again and again, and Gao Huan came to know the name.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was specially appointed flying-cavalry general and governor of Fanyang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was specially appointed flying-cavalry general and governor of Fanyang.

literal: In the commandery he showed virtue and kindness.
idiomatic: In the commandery he governed with virtue and kindness.

literal: He died before Wenwei.
idiomatic: He died before his father Wenwei.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs in You and Ping provinces, governor of You Province, and minister of revenue; posthumous title Ding.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, supervision of military affairs in You and Ping provinces, governorship of You Province, and the ministry of revenue; posthumous title Ding, "Settled."

literal: His son Xunzu inherited his grandfather's title, Baron of Daxia.
idiomatic: His son Xunzu inherited his grandfather's title, baron of Daxia.

literal: He had expertise in arts and learning; his writings were florid and ornate — a brilliant man among the younger generation.
idiomatic: Trained in the arts and sciences, he wrote in a florid, ornate style, and stood among the finest of the younger generation.

literal: Recommended as a provincial graduate, he entered the capital.
idiomatic: Recommended as a provincial graduate, he went to the capital.

literal: Li Zuxun once held a banquet for men of letters; Emperor Xianzu sent a palace attendant eunuch to instruct Zuxun: "The Rouran have been destroyed — why is there no congratulatory memorial?
idiomatic: Li Zuxun once gathered men of letters for a feast; Gao Yang sent a palace attendant with an order for Zuxun: "The Rouran are broken — where is your congratulatory memorial?

literal: The messenger stood waiting.
idiomatic: The messenger stood waiting.

literal: All the guests drafted memorials; Xunzu finished his in no time.
idiomatic: Every guest set to drafting a memorial; Xunzu finished his in moments.

literal: Later the court made mass appointments and promotions, summoning men to take office on the same day.
idiomatic: Later the court issued a wave of appointments, summoning men to take office all on the same day.

literal: Xunzu stood outside the East Gate Where Chariots Stop and drafted memorials for more than twenty men — his text needed no correction, and the language and reasoning were admirable.
idiomatic: Xunzu stood outside the East Gate Where Chariots Stop and drafted memorials for more than twenty men — not a word to revise, the language clear and the reasoning sound.

literal: When Xunzu first inherited the title and was enfeoffed Baron of Daxia, an elder statesman of long standing said to him: "Great Summer is just forming."
idiomatic: When Xunzu first inherited his title as baron of Daxia, an elder statesman of long standing said to him: "Great Summer is just taking shape."

literal: He answered on the spot: "For now let the sparrows and swallows congratulate one another."
idiomatic: He answered at once: "For now let sparrow and swallow congratulate each other."

literal: At the end of Tianbao, because of his office he was sent out as sub-official in charge of building the Long Wall.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, by virtue of his office he was sent out as sub-official in charge of building the Long Wall.

literal: Proud of his talent and inwardly resentful, he disheveled his appearance and dressed like a menial laborer to see Yang Yin.
idiomatic: Proud of his gifts and smoldering inside, he disheveled his dress and appeared like a common laborer when he went to see Yang Yin.

literal: Yin said: "Old friends have all been given posts — only Great Summer has received no appointment."
idiomatic: Yang Yin said: "Every old friend has been given a post — only Great Summer has not."

literal: Xunzu said in a harsh voice: "Whose fault is that!"
idiomatic: Xunzu cried out: "Whose fault is that!"

literal: Once he reached his posting, he composed "Rhapsody on Building the Long Wall," which in part reads: "Planks of purple cypress, pestles of papaya — what sort of timber for what sort of use?"
idiomatic: Once at his posting he wrote "Rhapsody on Building the Long Wall," which in part reads: "Planks of purple cypress, pestles of papaya — what timber for what task?"

literal: "Grass grows lush and tangled, clinging to the hillsides; if only every ten paces there were a fragrant bloom, I would have no quarrel with dwelling among thorns."
idiomatic: "Grass grows lush and tangled along the hills — if only every ten paces held a fragrant bloom, I would have no complaint about dwelling among thorns."

literal: Xing Shao once joked: "You are young and your talent and learning abundant — horned beasts have no upper teeth; I fear you will not live long."
idiomatic: Xing Shao once teased him: "You are young and your talent runs deep — but horned beasts have no upper teeth; I fear you will not live long."

literal: He replied: "When Xunzu first heard these words, I truly felt fear — but seeing you, elder, with gray hair at your temples, I am somewhat reassured."
idiomatic: He replied: "When I first heard that, I was genuinely afraid — but seeing your temples gone gray, elder, I take some comfort."

literal: Shao greatly valued his quick wit.
idiomatic: Shao greatly admired his quick wit.

literal: Endowed with eloquence, he loved to praise and blame others; he once told someone: "Yesterday, before dawn, passing outside the He family gate, I already saw two Lus and two Yuans, standing tall alongside the locust trees and willows."
idiomatic: Gifted with a sharp tongue, he loved to pass judgment on others; he once told someone: "Yesterday, before dawn, I passed the He family gate and already saw two Lus and two Yuans standing tall as locust and willow."

literal: He meant Yan Shi and Renhui, and Wenzong and Nayan; Xing Shao lavishly praised Lu Sidao and held that Xunzu fell short.
idiomatic: He meant Lu Yan Shi and Lu Renhui, and Yuan Wenzong and Yuan Nayan; Xing Shao lavishly praised Lu Sidao and judged Xunzu the lesser man.

literal: Xunzu said: "Those who see one unable to soar high borrow him their feathers; those who know one whose momentum would pierce the sky clip his wings."
idiomatic: Xunzu said: "Those who see a man who cannot yet soar lend him their feathers; those who know a man whose momentum would pierce the sky clip his wings."

literal: Slander reached him day by day, and public opinion generally held his character in low esteem.
idiomatic: Slander reached him day by day, and public opinion turned against his character.

literal: Xing Ziguang, governor of Changguang, sized up the two Lus and said: "Xunzu has the self-restraint of Mi Heng; Sidao lacks the icy edge of Kong Rong."
idiomatic: Xing Ziguang, governor of Changguang, sized up the two Lus and said: "Xunzu has the self-restraint of Mi Heng; Sidao lacks the icy edge of Kong Rong."

literal: Later he somewhat restrained his conduct.
idiomatic: Later he somewhat restrained his conduct.

literal: He served as aide to the heir apparent and recorder of the chancellor's office, and died in office.
idiomatic: He served as aide to the heir apparent and recorder of the chancellor's office, and died in office.

literal: He had a collected writings in ten scrolls, all now lost.
idiomatic: He left a collected writings in ten scrolls, all now lost.

literal: He once composed dirge lyrics for Princess of Zhao Commandery, Lady Zheng, of which one piece reads: "The sovereign's dominion fills the seas; consorts and pairs fill the realm.
idiomatic: He once composed dirge lyrics for Princess of Zhao Commandery, Lady Zheng; one piece reads: "The sovereign's dominion fills the seas; consorts and pairs fill the realm.

literal: A woman's propriety eclipses the state of Zheng; a consort's grace outshines the palace of Zhao.
idiomatic: A woman's propriety eclipses the state of Zheng; a consort's grace outshines the palace of Zhao.

literal: Spring dyes the peach-blossom waters; autumn rides the cassia-branch winds.
idiomatic: Spring dyes the peach-blossom waters; autumn rides the cassia-branch winds.

literal: And so on the night at the Cluster Terrace, bright moon filled the empty bed."
idiomatic: And so on the night at the Cluster Terrace, bright moon filled the empty bed."

literal: Gongdao's younger brother Huaidao was light and impulsive, fond of wine, and possessed considerable ambition; for merit in holding Fanyang he entered service as supernumerary attendant cavalry.
idiomatic: Gongdao's younger brother Huaidao was light and impulsive, fond of wine, and ambitious; for merit in holding Fanyang he entered service as supernumerary attendant cavalry.

literal: Wenwei dispatched him to deliver a memorial to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Lu Wenwei dispatched him to deliver a memorial to Gao Huan.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made general who pacifies the west and grand master of splendid happiness.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made general who pacifies the west and grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the mobile headquarters submitted a memorial appointing him acting administrator of Ping Province affairs; for merit he went to the Overlord's headquarters.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the mobile headquarters submitted a memorial appointing him acting administrator of Ping Province affairs; for merit he went to the overlord's headquarters.

literal: During Xinghe he administered Fen Province affairs.
idiomatic: During Xinghe he administered Fen Province affairs.

literal: Huaidao's family had joined in raising the righteous banner; the Grand Ancestor treated him with personal favor and sent him out as garrison commander of Wusu, where he died in office.
idiomatic: Huaidao's family had joined in raising the righteous banner; Gao Huan treated him with personal favor and sent him out as garrison commander of Wusu, where he died in office.

literal: Huaidao's younger brother Zongdao was coarse and impulsive by nature, and heavily valued chivalric loyalty.
idiomatic: Huaidao's younger brother Zongdao was coarse and impulsive by nature, and heavily valued chivalric loyalty.

literal: He served as master of writing and attendant at court with regular attendance, and later acted as governor of Southern Ying Province.
idiomatic: He served as master of writing and attendant at court with regular attendance, and later acted as governor of Southern Ying Province.

literal: He once set out wine at Jinyang; guests and companions filled the hall.
idiomatic: He once set out wine at Jinyang; guests and companions filled the hall.

literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant Ma Shida eyed his female konghou player and said: "Her hands are very slender and fair."
idiomatic: Palace secretariat attendant Ma Shida eyed his female konghou player and said: "Her hands are very slender and fair."

literal: Zongdao immediately gave this maid to Shida; Shida firmly declined, so Zongdao ordered his household to cut off her wrist — Shida had no choice but to accept her.
idiomatic: Zongdao immediately gave the maid to Shida; Shida firmly declined, so Zongdao ordered his household to cut off her wrist — Shida had no choice but to accept her.

literal: About to depart for Ying Province, he gathered the district folk at the Dukang Dam, slaughtered cattle, and held a great feast.
idiomatic: About to depart for Ying Province, he gathered the district folk at the Dukang Dam, slaughtered cattle, and held a great feast.

literal: An old student, drunk, let slip some improper words in conversation; Zongdao thereupon ordered him drowned in the water.
idiomatic: An old student, drunk, let slip some improper words; Zongdao thereupon ordered him drowned.

literal: Later, for cruelty and excess he was dismissed and stripped of rank.
idiomatic: Later, for cruelty and excess he was dismissed and stripped of rank.

literal: Wenwei's clansman Yong, styled Jili, had a father Bi who was governor of Xiapi in Wei.
idiomatic: Lu Wenwei's clansman Yong, styled Jili, had a father Bi who was governor of Xiapi in Wei.

literal: In youth Yong and his elder cousin Jingyu were both in school; their uncle Tong praised them: "The white-haired one will surely excel in letters; Jili will surely reach distinction in arms — the raising of our house rests on these two."
idiomatic: In youth Yong and his elder cousin Jingyu were both in school; their uncle Tong praised them: "The white-haired one will surely excel in letters; Jili will surely reach distinction in arms — the raising of our house rests on these two."

literal: Pugu Na, rebel of You Province, made Yong prince of Fanyang in his native commandery when Yong was eighteen.
idiomatic: Pugu Na, rebel of You Province, made Yong prince of Fanyang in his native commandery when Yong was eighteen.

literal: Later, when Ge Rong raised disorder, Yong was again made Prince of Yan.
idiomatic: Later, when Ge Rong raised disorder, Yong was again made Prince of Yan.

literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Lu Wenwei summoned him, but he did not respond.
idiomatic: When the righteous banner was raised, Lu Wenwei summoned him, but he did not respond.

literal: Only after the Erzhu were destroyed did he go to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Only after the Erzhu were destroyed did he go to Jinyang.

literal: The Grand Ancestor appointed Yong chief clerk to the chancellor.
idiomatic: Gao Huan appointed Yong chief clerk to the chancellor.

literal: At that time the west of the mountains suffered frost and famine; rent grain from the east was transported in — all were ordered to load full measure, with punishment for violators; Yong was put in charge of the matter.
idiomatic: At that time the west of the mountains suffered frost and famine; rent grain from the east was transported in — all were ordered to load full measure, with punishment for violators; Yong was put in charge.

literal: The Princess of Langye falsely claimed more than a thousand carts; Yong impeached her.
idiomatic: The Princess of Langye falsely claimed more than a thousand carts; Yong impeached her.

literal: The princess appealed to the Grand Ancestor, but Yong upheld the law and would not yield.
idiomatic: The princess appealed to Gao Huan, but Yong upheld the law and would not yield.

literal: The Grand Ancestor told Guo Xiu: "Lu Yong has an unyielding, inviolable bearing — a truly upright man; he should be entrusted with great affairs, not merely collecting rent."
idiomatic: Gao Huan told Guo Xiu: "Lu Yong has an unyielding, inviolable bearing — a truly upright man; he should be entrusted with great affairs, not merely collecting rent."

literal: He was transferred to governor of Rubei, administered Shaan Province affairs, and then administered Luo Province affairs.
idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Rubei, administered Shaan Province affairs, and then administered Luo Province affairs.

literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang, the imperial army besieged Guangzhou for several tens of days without taking it.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxiang, the imperial army besieged Guangzhou for several tens of days without taking it.

literal: Mobile headquarters commander Hou Jing, hearing that Western Wei relief troops were about to arrive, gathered the generals to deliberate.
idiomatic: Mobile headquarters commander Hou Jing, hearing that Western Wei relief troops were about to arrive, gathered the generals to deliberate.

literal: Yong went forward to observe the situation; thereupon he led a hundred horsemen, each covering one horse with a cage.
idiomatic: Yong went forward to observe the situation; thereupon he led a hundred horsemen, each covering one horse with a cage.

literal: Reaching Mount Dawei, he learned that Wei general Li Jinghe was leading an army and would soon arrive.
idiomatic: Reaching Mount Dawei, he learned that Wei general Li Jinghe was leading an army and would soon arrive.

literal: Yong planted many banners and flags in the treetops, divided his cavalry into ten squads, sounded horns and charged straight ahead, captured Western Wei acting third-grade-equal Li Chenghua, beheaded acting third-grade-equal Wang Zhengman, drove off three hundred horses, and returned through the night.
idiomatic: Yong planted many banners and flags in the treetops, divided his cavalry into ten squads, sounded horns and charged straight ahead, captured Western Wei acting third-grade-equal Li Chenghua, beheaded acting third-grade-equal Wang Zhengman, drove off three hundred horses, and returned through the night.

literal: Guangzhou's defending commander Luo Chao surrendered the city; the Grand Ancestor appointed Yong to administer Guangzhou affairs.
idiomatic: Guangzhou's defending commander Luo Chao surrendered the city; Gao Huan appointed Yong to administer Guangzhou affairs.

literal: For merit he was granted acting third-grade-equal, governor of Yang Province, and garrisoned at Yiyang.
idiomatic: For merit he was granted acting third-grade-equal, governor of Yang Province, and garrisoned at Yiyang.

literal: Rebel commoners Han Mulan, Chen Xin, and others were constant border troubles; Yong routed them utterly.
idiomatic: Rebel commoners Han Mulan, Chen Xin, and others were constant border troubles; Yong routed them utterly.

literal: He submitted a memorial requesting to enter court; the Grand Ancestor sent Yong a letter: "I have entrusted Yang Province to you — you need only sleep with pillow high and lie at ease, with no worries from the southwest.
idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting to enter court; Gao Huan sent Yong a letter: "I have entrusted Yang Province to you — you need only sleep with pillow high and lie at ease, with no worries from the southwest.

literal: But as the court has entrusted you, memorials and reports should cease.
idiomatic: But as the court has entrusted you, memorials and reports should cease.

literal: Your wife and children may remain in the province; among the Han children there shall be none who rank above you."
idiomatic: Your wife and children may remain in the province; among the Han children there shall be none who rank above you."

literal: In the second year of Wuding he died, aged thirty-two.
idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he died, aged thirty-two.

literal: Yong had five hundred horses and six carts of armor and weapons freshly made; in his final memorial he presented them all to the court.
idiomatic: Yong had five hundred horses and six carts of armor and weapons freshly made; in his final memorial he presented them all to the court.

literal: Beyond the funeral gifts, he was separately granted four thousand bolts of cloth and silk.
idiomatic: Beyond the funeral gifts, he was separately granted four thousand bolts of cloth and silk.

literal: Posthumously granted minister of works, governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Marquis Wuzhen.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted minister of works and governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Marquis Wuzhen.

literal: Li Yishen was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.
idiomatic: Li Yishen was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.

literal: His grandfather Zhen was attendant master of writing in Wei.
idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was attendant master of writing in Wei.

literal: His father Shaozong was administrative aide of Yin Province.
idiomatic: His father Shaozong was administrative aide of Yin Province.

literal: Yishen's learning ranged across the classics and histories; he possessed talent useful to his age.
idiomatic: Yishen's learning ranged across the classics and histories; he possessed talent useful to his age.

literal: He began office as merit officer of the eastern campaign staff of Ji Province and was repeatedly promoted to flying-cavalry general.
idiomatic: He began office as merit officer of the eastern campaign staff of Ji Province and was repeatedly promoted to flying-cavalry general.

literal: When the righteous banner was first raised, he joined the Grand Ancestor at Xindu and was made master of writing of the great mobile headquarters.
idiomatic: When the righteous banner was first raised, he joined Gao Huan at Xindu and was made master of writing of the great mobile headquarters.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the south and vice minister of the court of imperial entertainments.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the south and vice minister of the court of imperial entertainments.

literal: Yishen saw that Erzhu Zhao's troops were strong and thereupon rebelled against the Grand Ancestor and fled to join him.
idiomatic: Yishen saw that Erzhu Zhao's troops were strong and thereupon rebelled against Gao Huan and fled to join him.

literal: When Zhao was pacified, the Grand Ancestor pardoned his crime and made him recorder of the great chancellor's government office.
idiomatic: When Zhao was pacified, Gao Huan pardoned his crime and made him recorder of the great chancellor's government office.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness and chancellor's marshal; in every post he was praised as competent.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness and chancellor's marshal; in every post he was praised as competent.

literal: He was transferred to chief administrator of Bing Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of Bing Province.

literal: At that time Governor Kezhun Hun Daoyuan did not attend to minor affairs; civil matters were largely entrusted to Yishen, who handled them with great dispatch.
idiomatic: At that time Governor Kezhun Hun Daoyuan did not attend to minor affairs; civil matters were largely entrusted to Yishen, who handled them with great dispatch.

literal: He again served as the great chancellor's marshal.
idiomatic: He again served as the great chancellor's marshal.

literal: During Wuding he was appointed governor of Qi Province; he was fond of wealth and profit and accepted many bribes.
idiomatic: During Wuding he was appointed governor of Qi Province; he was fond of wealth and profit and accepted many bribes.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he administered Zheng Province affairs, then administered Liang Province affairs; soon he was appointed attendant cavalry with regular attendance and made governor of Yangxia.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he administered Zheng Province affairs, then administered Liang Province affairs; soon he was appointed attendant cavalry with regular attendance and made governor of Yangxia.

literal: Duan Ye reported that he had amassed wealth in the province; he was placed under arrest, sent to Liang Province for thorough investigation, and the case was not yet concluded.
idiomatic: Duan Ye reported that he had amassed wealth in the province; he was placed under arrest, sent to Liang Province for thorough investigation, and the case was not yet concluded.

literal: In the third year he fell ill and died in confinement, aged fifty-seven.
idiomatic: In the third year he fell ill and died in confinement, aged fifty-seven.

literal: His son Taotao was talented and eloquent; he served as master of writing and magistrate of Ye County, and at the beginning of Wuping concurrently held attendant at court with regular attendance.
idiomatic: His son Taotao was talented and eloquent; he served as master of writing and magistrate of Ye County, and at the beginning of Wuping concurrently held attendant at court with regular attendance.

literal: Sent on a mission to Chen, he was praised by the men of Chen.
idiomatic: Sent on a mission to Chen, he was praised by the men of Chen.
